Compare latent classes on an external outcome

Source: R/three-step.R
three_step.Rd

three_step() estimates how an outcome that was not used to define the classes differs between them, holding the measurement model fixed so the classes keep their meaning. Comparing classes by modal assignment treats uncertain assignments as certain and biases the differences; the three-step methods correct for the classification error of the fitted model. The default is the Bolck-Croon-Hagenaars ("bch") weighting; the maximum-likelihood ("ml") method models the outcome given the true class instead. Both assume that the outcome and the assigned class are independent given the true class; the differences are associations, not effects of class membership.

Usage

three_step(
  x,
  data,
  outcome,
  level = c("individuals", "groups"),
  method = c("bch", "proportional", "modal", "ml"),
  ci_level = 0.95,
  contrast = c("none", "pairs", "overall"),
  adjust = c("BH", "holm", "hochberg", "hommel", "bonferroni", "BY", "none"),
  vcov_type = c("cluster", "independent"),
  variance = c("varying", "equal"),
  step_one = c("fixed", "estimated")
)

Arguments

x

A covariate-free fit: from multilpa() (the profile family), from lta() with its default homogeneous first-order transitions and invariant measurement, or a trajectory model that classifies persons (mixture_regression() with class_level = "group", with or without random) fitted without membership covariates. Refused: fits with membership covariates, multilevel growth mixtures (cluster), the other multilpa() families, observation-level mixture regressions, fits with weights or a noise component, and lta() fits with occasion-specific or covariate transitions, second order, occasion- specific measurement, a stayer class or ordinal or count indicators.

data

The data frame carrying the outcome, in the fit's row order; columns shared with the fit are checked row by row. For a trajectory model, the data the model was fitted to.

outcome

Name of the outcome column, without missing or infinite values and not an indicator of x: numeric for class means, or a factor, character or logical column for the probability of each category in each class. For level = "groups" it must be constant within each group; for a trajectory model, within each person.

level

"individuals" (default) relates the outcome to the profiles, "groups" to the group classes. A trajectory model relates it to its person classes, reported as level = "persons".

method

"bch" (default): Bolck-Croon-Hagenaars weights. "ml": the maximum-likelihood step-three model. "proportional": posterior weights without correction. "modal": modal assignment without correction. See Methods.

ci_level

Confidence level of the intervals (default 0.95).

contrast

"none" (default): one outcome mean per class (one probability per class and category). "pairs": the difference between every pair of classes, tested against zero. "overall": one Wald test that every class has the same mean (the same category distribution).

adjust

Multiplicity correction across the pairwise differences, a stats::p.adjust() method; "BH" by default. Ignored for contrast = "none" or "overall". With a binary outcome, its two complementary category rows count as one test per class pair; with more categories, every reported category difference enters the family.

vcov_type

"cluster" (default) treats the fit's groups as the independent units of the sandwich variance, as the nesting requires; "independent" treats every observation as independent.

variance

For method = "ml" with a numeric outcome (refused otherwise): "varying" (default) estimates an outcome variance in each class, "equal" one shared by the classes.

step_one

"fixed" (default) conditions on the step-one estimates. "estimated" adds the uncertainty of the classification-error probabilities (and, under "ml", of the class sizes) to the step-three covariance; available for lpa(), lca() and multilpa() profile fits at either level when their Wald inference is available and their measurement was estimated jointly. Staged fits and fits holding a measurement block fixed are refused. See Step-one uncertainty.

Value

A data frame. For contrast = "none", one row per class (per class and category for a categorical outcome, with category after class): level, method, class, estimate, standard_error, conf_low, conf_high and effective_n; means are not tested, and a probability's interval is formed on the logit scale. Under method = "ml" with a numeric outcome a variance column precedes effective_n, and under "ml" effective_n is the expected number of units in the class. For contrast = "pairs", one row per pair (per pair and category): level, method, class, reference_class, estimate (class minus reference), standard_error, statistic, p_value, p_adjusted, conf_low and conf_high, as in r3step(). For contrast = "overall", one row: level, method, statistic, df (K - 1 for a mean, (K - 1)(C - 1) for C categories) and p_value. The attributes vcov_type and step_one record the choices, adjust on a pairs result and variance on a numeric ML result with contrast = "none".

Methods

BCH gives each observation one weight per class, the row of the inverse classification-error matrix for its assigned class, and takes weighted means. With method = "ml" the assigned class is an indicator of the true class with the step-one error probabilities, and the outcome is normal within each true class (a multinomial distribution for a categorical outcome), with the class sizes fixed at the average posteriors, as in Latent GOLD's step-three model. The likelihood is maximised from a fixed set of starts plus twenty seeded random ones, so the result does not depend on the caller's seed; the global maximum is not guaranteed. ML depends on the within-class outcome distribution: skewness or a wrong equal-variance constraint can bias the means, and BCH is less sensitive to that.

A categorical outcome is described by its probability in each class. BCH weights can be negative, so with poorly separated classes a share can fall outside 0 to 1; it is then reported without an interval or test, with a warning. The ML probabilities stay in range; where the BCH shares do not, the ML maximum usually sits on the bound and is reported without standard errors, with a warning.

On an lta() fit, level = "individuals" uses one row per occasion and relates the outcome to the profile at that occasion, with the group-clustered variance accounting for the repeated occasions. It is a marginal profile-outcome analysis, not a model of outcome effects on transitions.

Standard errors

The variance is a sandwich over the G independent units (the groups, or the observations under vcov_type = "independent") with the G / (G - 1) small-sample factor. It needs more units than classes; with as many or fewer, the analysis is refused. A class carried by one unit (Kish's effective number of units carrying it below 1.5) has no standard error: its interval and the contrasts involving it are NA, with a warning.

Step-one uncertainty

With step_one = "fixed" the intervals ignore the uncertainty of the classification-error probabilities, which lowers their coverage when classification is uncertain. "estimated" adds the first-order contribution of the step-one covariance, with the data and modal assignments held fixed; the estimates are unchanged, the standard errors and intervals grow, and the tests use the corrected covariance. The first-stage contribution uses its model-based observed information, even when the step-three sandwich is clustered; it does not add a robust first-stage covariance for residual dependence outside the fitted model. The correction is a large-sample one: in a small, poorly separated sample the intervals still cover less than the nominal level. The modal method is unaffected, as it uses no posteriors. A staged fit or a fit with a held measurement block does not carry the measurement covariance needed by this correction; use step_one = "fixed" to report inference conditional on that measurement. Neither option includes the uncertainty of having selected the class solution.

See also

r3step() for covariates of class membership; fit_staged().

Examples

set.seed(11)
group <- rep(seq_len(40), each = 10)
truth <- 1L + as.integer(runif(400) > 0.5)
example_data <- data.frame(
  g = group,
  a = rnorm(400, ifelse(truth == 2L, 1.1, -1.1)),
  b = rnorm(400, ifelse(truth == 2L, 1.1, -1.1)),
  y = rnorm(400, ifelse(truth == 2L, 10, 0))
)
fit <- multilpa(example_data, c("a", "b"), "g", n_profiles = 2,
                n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 4, seed = 1)
three_step(fit, example_data, "y")
#> Distal outcome by class (bch, 95% CI)
#> 
#> Class    Mean            95% CI    SE  Effective n
#> -----  ------  ----------------  ----  -----------
#>     1  -0.069  [-0.463,  0.325]  0.20       182.74
#>     2   9.972  [ 9.531, 10.412]  0.22       170.37
three_step(fit, example_data, "y", contrast = "pairs")
#> Distal outcome: class differences (bch, 95% CI)
#> 
#> Class  vs  Difference         95% CI      p  p (BH)
#> -----  --  ----------  -------------  -----  ------
#>     2   1       10.04  [9.37, 10.72]  <.001   <.001
# A categorical outcome: its probability in each class.
example_data <- transform(example_data, passed = y + rnorm(400, sd = 6) > 5)
three_step(fit, example_data, "passed")
#> Distal outcome by class (bch, 95% CI)
#> 
#> Class  Category  Probability        95% CI     SE  Effective n
#> -----  --------  -----------  ------------  -----  -----------
#>     1  FALSE            0.80  [0.73, 0.85]  0.030       182.74
#>     1  TRUE             0.20  [0.15, 0.27]  0.030       182.74
#>     2  FALSE            0.17  [0.12, 0.23]  0.030       170.37
#>     2  TRUE             0.83  [0.77, 0.88]  0.030       170.37
three_step(fit, example_data, "passed", contrast = "overall")
#> Distal outcome: equal across classes (bch, Wald)
#> 
#>  Wald  df      p
#> -----  --  -----
#> 99.11   1  <.001
